problem: Transformer-based VLN agents summarize temporal context in a single fixed-length vector (LSTM state or recurrent hidden state), which is too weak to capture long-term cross-modal history and align it with sub-instructions. Visual-only history encoders miss instruction-observation interactions.
motivation: VLN requires the agent to know which part of the instruction is completed and what comes next, so temporal context is key for grounding. Explicitly storing past cross-modal activations lets the Transformer take variable-length history without a separate recurrent network.
key_idea: Store the cross-modal Transformer output activation of the chosen action at every step in a growing memory bank fed back as input tokens, and regularize with a memory-aware consistency loss between full and randomly word-dropped instructions.
insight: Explicit cross-modal history tokens beat both recurrent state and visual-only history encoders (Table 3: 65.7 SR val-unseen vs 63 for VLN-BERT, 63.5 for HAMT, 59.0 for E.T.). Larger memory helps and variable-length is best (Fig. 4). The consistency loss adds +1.7 SR / +0.8 SPL over the no-consistency model, while plain word-dropping augmentation gives only +0.5 SR and -0.8 SPL, so the gain comes from the KL consistency rather than word dropping itself.
method: Memory bank: after each step, append the output activation of the selected action's view, concatenated with its directional feature, to memory M_t; the memory grows with the trajectory (variable length).

Cross-modality encoder: a LXMERT/PREVALENT-style encoder with self- and cross-attention takes instruction X and [M_t; V_t] (memory plus candidate visual features) and an MLP on the visual outputs predicts the action.
Vision/language encoders: ResNet-152 (Places365) features 2048-d plus 128-d direction feature per view; a multi-layer Transformer language encoder initialized from PREVALENT.

Memory-aware consistency loss: randomly drop instruction words (p=0.5), run both the full and dropped instruction through the encoders, and minimize bidirectional KL between the language-encoder outputs (λs) and between the cross-modal outputs (λm).

Training: mix of imitation learning and A2C RL with rewards for goal success, distance reduction and path similarity; consistency loss applied in both; initialized from PREVALENT and trained with augmented data; AdamW, lr 5e-6.

setting.backbone: PREVALENT-initialized cross-modal Transformer (fine-tuned) with ResNet-152 visual features
setting.training_data: R2R original training data plus PREVALENT augmented data; CVDN training set; PREVALENT pretraining

numbers_note: Table 1 reports integer-rounded SR/SPL; Table 3/4 give one-decimal val-unseen values. Memory-size ablation results are only in figures. Paper text has inconsistent hyperparameter values (λs=0.6, λm=0.2 in the implementation details vs 6 and 2 in the sensitivity analysis).
results: MTVM achieves 66 SR / 59 SPL on R2R val-unseen and 65 SR / 59 SPL on R2R test, beating VLN-BERT (63/57 val-unseen, 63/57 test). On CVDN test, Goal Progress is 4.23/4.46/4.82 m (Oracle/Navigator/Mixed), versus 2.77/3.37/3.31 for the strongest baselines DR-Attacker and SCoA.
limitations: Memory grows with trajectory length, and the model is heavier (68.4M params, 17.9GB vs 8.6GB for VLN-BERT) due to bidirectional cross-attention; R2R paths are short (4-6 steps), so long-horizon behavior is untested.
Relies on PREVALENT pretraining and augmented data; evaluated only on discrete-graph R2R/CVDN.
Gains over baselines are modest (~2 points) and the memory-size analysis is given only as figures.
